name: Shakti back-and-forth: both signals reversed, then corrected
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti software), after Persinger's vectorial hemisphericity theory
summary: Option 2 of Murphy's back-and-forth session: 30 min with the amygdala signal on the right and the hippocampal signal on the left (both on their 'usually wrong' sides), then 30 min with both on their usual sides (amygdala left, hippocampus right). Murphy says the first phase is expected to be unpleasant.
setting: Advanced users only, after a side test has shown the usual pattern for the signal (this file assumes the usual sides). The vendor says darkness and silence (sensory deprivation) help; eyes closed, relaxed. Test both signals first (murphy-shakti-test-session-amygdala and -hippocampus, at least 72 hours apart).
schedule: Vendor rules: never on consecutive days, at most every 72 hours or weekly; 60-minute sessions at most once in 3 weeks.
notes: The vendor's option 2 'reverses both signals, then corrects both'; running the two signals at the same time, one on each side, is this project's reading (an inference). Murphy bases the design on Persinger's vectorial hemisphericity idea: stimulating a structure's negative counterpart first mutes the positive one, and stimulating the positive one next gives what he calls a 'sudden burst'. The left/right rules rest on user reports and small Persinger-lab studies (Richards, Koren & Persinger 1992; Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994). Murphy links the right amygdala with fear and sadness and the left hippocampus with irritability, mostly from user reports, so phase 1 can bring fear or irritability. Phase 1 is meant to be unpleasant (the vendor: 'EXPECTED to be unpleasant') and phase 2 pleasant; if phase 1 feels good instead, the vendor reads that as a possible 'reversed' or 'left-handed' structure. The vendor offers this option only after the single-signal procedure, which it 'strongly' suggests running with each signal separately first (murphy-shakti-back-and-forth-amygdala and -hippocampus). If phase 1 becomes too uncomfortable, press Skip at once to start phase 2, but never stop after phase 1 without phase 2 (the vendor: 'Do NOT apply the signal over the wrong side without following it with the same signal over the correct side'). For unwanted effects that linger, the vendor's undo procedures are the hippocampal signal over both frontal lobes or the ERP signal over the cerebellum (in this project: murphy-shakti-cerebellum-erp). Coils: a cross of four over each temporal lobe (FT7, C5, TP7, T9 and FT8, C6, TP8, T10); in each phase one track drives the four coils of one side with one signal, without movement or channel alternation (none is described for this procedure). The burst repeats every 4.69 s and the LTP train every 4.74 s, so the two drift against each other. The Alternative procedures page gives this option as 'Reversing both signals for 30 minutes, followed by applying both signals to the 'correct' sides for 30 minutes' (the Bliss page gives 20-30 min per phase). The amygdala ('burstx') file is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points at the vendor's standard 3-ms points (0.69 s), followed by the vendor's standard latency of about 4 s. The hippocampal 'LTP' file is proprietary; it is approximated by a point table in the vendor's standard scheme (3-ms points, about 4 s of latency): four theta bursts, each of four biphasic pulses 9 ms apart (after the 4-pulse bursts of Larson & Lynch 1986), one burst every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal). The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% with hippocampal signals; if so, lower the intensity by one third. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy, seizure history or a psychiatric condition. If phase 1 is distressing, skip to phase 2 as the vendor advises; stop the session if distress continues in phase 2. Revised after a re-check of the procedures page (2026): the page's advice on order and on 'reversed' structures is added; sites, signals and timing are unchanged and remain approximations as described.

phases.name: Phase 1: amygdala RIGHT + hippocampus LEFT (both reversed)
Phase 2: amygdala LEFT + hippocampus RIGHT (both corrected)
